incident_spec.summary: Investigating the performance and concurrency behavior of large transactions in PostgreSQL.
symptoms: Blocked transactions when attempting to update rows locked by another transaction.
Potential serialization errors in higher isolation levels.
incident_spec.mechanism: PostgreSQL's MVCC (Multiversion Concurrency Control) model and transaction isolation levels determine the behavior of concurrent transactions and their impact on performance.

facts.key: MVCC allows reads and writes to not block each other.
facts.evidence: Postgres documentation on MVCC and concurrency control.

facts.key: Transactions can block each other when attempting to update the same rows.
facts.evidence: Example provided in the DBA post with two sessions updating the same row.

facts.key: Higher isolation levels can lead to serialization errors.
facts.evidence: Postgres documentation on transaction isolation levels.

assumptions: The PostgreSQL version used for reproduction will behave similarly to version 9.3 as described in the post.
The synthetic data and workload will sufficiently mimic the described scenario to reproduce the behavior.
unknowns: Exact schema and data distribution of the original database.
Whether the issue is specific to PostgreSQL 9.3 or generalizable to other versions.

feasibility.rationale: The reproduction focuses on PostgreSQL's MVCC and transaction isolation mechanisms, which are well-documented and can be simulated with synthetic data.

schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tools (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, description TEXT);
generation_sql: INSERT INTO tools (description) SELECT CONCAT('tool_', g.i) FROM generate_series(1, {row_count}) AS g(i);

tables.name: tools
tables.purpose: Simulate a table with rows being updated and read during transactions.
tables.distribution_notes: Uniform distribution of rows with unique IDs.

calibration_queries.objective: Verify that the table and data are correctly set up for the experiment.
expected_evidence: The query retrieves the row with id = 1.
The row's description matches the expected value.

queries.sql: BEGIN; UPDATE tools SET description = 'updated_tool' WHERE id = 1; -- Simulate a long transaction
BEGIN; UPDATE tools SET description = 'conflicting_update' WHERE id = 1; -- Simulate a conflicting transaction

validation_criteria: Transaction conflicts are observed when two transactions attempt to update the same row.
The second transaction is blocked until the first transaction commits or rolls back.
symptom_evidence: Blocked transactions when attempting to update rows locked by another transaction.
Potential serialization errors in higher isolation levels.
mechanism_evidence: PostgreSQL's MVCC model allows reads to proceed during writes.
Transaction isolation levels affect the behavior of concurrent transactions.
